newsitem.title: USA: SEC seeks changes to system that links markets-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: SEC seeks changes to system that links markets-WSJ.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission is pushing stock markets in the United States to change what it considers to be the "anticompetitive" aspects of the trading system that connects them, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.
The Journal said the SEC sent a letter on May 27 contending that certain rules set by the Intermarket Trading System, a consortium of all the markets, puts some members at a disadvantage.

The SEC said in the letter that it "has initiated ... a review concerning certain anticompetitive aspects of the Intermarket Trading System." It asked that regulatory officials from the member markets issue a proposal within 30 days for ways to fix the problems outlined in the letter.

The trading system links the order display systems of the New York, Nasdaq, American and regional stock exchanges, allowing brokers to tap into the best quotation for a New York Stock Exchange-listed stock, the Journal reported.

One tradomg system rule targeted by the SEC is one that prohibits stock quotes for certain stocks that were listed on the Big Board before 1979 to be accessible through the Intermarket Trading System via Nasdaq's trading system.

The SEC in the letter maintains that "this limitation on ITS access unreasonably reduces competition in the trading" of such older stocks "and decreases opportunities for best execution," the Journal reported.
